sentences.en: A landmark antitrust ruling against Google last week had at its heart the story of another case, one from the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 上周针对谷歌的一项里程碑式反垄断裁决，其核心是另一个案件的故事，一个源自20世纪90年代的案件。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Steve Lohr on the influence of U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事史蒂夫·洛尔将探讨美国诉

sentences.zh: 微软案

sentences.en: Microsoft and what lessons that case may hold for the future of big tech today.
sentences.zh: 的影响，以及该案对当今大型科技公司未来发展的启示。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月14日，星期三。

sentences.en: Steve, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Nice to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, Steve, we wanted to have you on the show because last week we finally got a decision in the big case involving Google.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫，我们想请你来做客，因为上周我们终于迎来了涉及谷歌的大案的判决。

sentences.en: And that was, of course, the case where the Department of Justice was arguing that Google was a monopoly.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是司法部指控谷歌为垄断企业的案件。

sentences.en: And as we now know, the judge in the case agreed.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所知，该案的法官表示赞同。

sentences.en: So, just to start, refresh our memories about this case.
sentences.zh: 那么，首先请帮我们回顾一下这个案件。

sentences.en: This is the first big anti-monopoly case against a modern tech company.
sentences.zh: 这是针对现代科技公司的首起大型反垄断案。

sentences.en: There are others in the works.
sentences.zh: 还有其他案件正在筹备中。

sentences.en: There's Amazon, Apple, and Meta, and those are to come.
sentences.zh: 包括亚马逊、苹果和Meta，这些都将陆续到来。

sentences.en: But this is the first salvo in this standoff between the antitrust enforcers and the big tech companies.
sentences.zh: 但这是反垄断执法人员与大型科技公司对峙的第一枪。

sentences.en: This one was actually filed in the Trump administration, but picked up with eagerness by the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 这个案件实际上是在特朗普政府时期提出的，但被拜登政府热切地接手了。

sentences.en: And it centers on search.
sentences.zh: 它以搜索为核心。

sentences.en: And the allegation here is that Google used its monopoly power to shut off competition and control distribution of its search engine to the disadvantage of everyone else.
sentences.zh: 其指控是，谷歌利用其垄断力量切断竞争，控制其搜索引擎的分发，从而损害了所有其他人的利益。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the way it did that, according to the government, was by paying companies like Apple, like Samsung, to be the default search engine on their platforMs.
sentences.zh: 根据政府的说法，它是通过向苹果、三星等公司付费，使其成为其平台上的默认搜索引擎来实现这一点的。

sentences.en: The DOJ, of course, said, this is illegal.
sentences.zh: 司法部理所当然地表示，这是非法的。

sentences.en: Google's response was, in essence, no, this is just good business.
sentences.zh: 谷歌的回应本质上是：不，这只是正常的商业行为。

sentences.en: These platforms want us there because we're the beSt.
sentences.zh: 这些平台希望我们在那里，因为我们是最好的。

sentences.en: And our customers see that.
sentences.zh: 我们的客户也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But the judge ruled in favor of the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 但法官作出了有利于司法部的裁决。

sentences.en: And one of the things I think is quite interesting about it is the continued, repeated references in the ruling to this case from the 1990s, US v.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中非常有趣的一点是，裁决中反复且持续地提及20世纪90年代的这个案件：美国诉

sentences.en: Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 微软案。

sentences.en: It's really clear that this is a template that the judge is working from, you know, this case that was the last time the government took on a big tech company and won.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这是法官正在遵循的模板，你知道，这个案件是政府最后一次起诉一家大型科技公司并获胜。

sentences.en: And Steve, we are very lucky to have you in studio with us today because you actually covered that case for The Times back in 1998.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫，我们今天非常幸运能请你来到演播室，因为你在1998年就曾为《时报》报道过那个案件。

sentences.en: So there's no one better to help us understand how that moment connects to this one.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人比你更适合帮助我们理解那个时刻是如何与现在相连的。

sentences.en: So let's start with a basic explanation of that Microsoft case.
sentences.zh: 让我们从对微软案的基本解释开始。

sentences.en: What do I need to know about it?
sentences.zh: 关于它我需要知道些什么？

sentences.en: Um, it was a huge trial.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一场巨大的审判。

sentences.en: This was the big showdown in the Clinton administration between the Department of Justice and Microsoft, which was by far the dominant technology company of its day.
sentences.zh: 这是克林顿政府时期司法部与微软之间的大对决，微软当时是无可争议的主导科技公司。

sentences.en: Just to paint the picture here.
sentences.zh: 为了描绘当时的画面。

sentences.en: I mean, in the early and mid-1990s, it is the personal computer era.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在20世纪90年代初期和中期，那是个人电脑时代。

sentences.en: Microsoft Windows operating system runs on more than 90% of the personal computers in the world.
sentences.zh: 微软的Windows操作系统运行在世界上90%以上的个人电脑上。

sentences.en: It shapes people's computing experience.
sentences.zh: 它塑造了人们的计算体验。

sentences.en: And it was more than that.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此。

sentences.en: They dominated this industry in a way that if you were a personal computer maker, you had to deal with Microsoft on their terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们主导这个行业的方式是，如果你是一家个人电脑制造商，你就必须按照微软的条件与他们打交道。

sentences.en: And the reason why Bill Gates at the time was, I think, neck and neck with Warren Buffett to be the richest man in the world, all of that was because of the Microsoft control of
sentences.zh: 当时比尔·盖茨之所以能与沃伦·巴菲特不相上下、争夺世界首富，原因全在于微软对

sentences.en: the personal computer industry.
sentences.zh: 个人电脑行业的控制。

sentences.en: And what really showed the reach and power of Microsoft and Bill Gates, both as an economic force and a cultural force, really came in 1995 with the introduction of a new version
sentences.zh: 真正展现微软和比尔·盖茨的影响力和力量（无论作为经济力量还是文化力量）是在1995年，当时推出了一种名为Windows 95的新版

sentences.en: of Windows called Windows 95.
sentences.zh: 本Windows。

sentences.en: Bill Gates is on his way into millions of American homes, through the windows.
sentences.zh: 比尔·盖茨正通过Windows走进千千万万美国家庭。

sentences.en: Windows 95, one of the most hyped consumer products ever.
sentences.zh: Windows 95是有史以来炒作最厉害的消费产品之一。

sentences.en: The debut of Windows 95, as nerdy as it was, was a cultural event.
sentences.zh: Windows 95的首次亮相虽然充满了极客气息，但却是一场文化盛事。

sentences.en: Welcome, Microsofties.
sentences.zh: 欢迎，微软迷们。

sentences.en: Nice to have you all here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴大家来到这里。

sentences.en: Actually, I'm here to tell you about this Windows 95.
sentences.zh: 其实，我是来向大家介绍这款Windows 95的。

sentences.en: Let me give you an idea.
sentences.zh: 让我给你们一个概念。

sentences.en: Give me an idea how powerful Windows 95 is.
sentences.zh: 让我给你们展示一下Windows 95有多强大。

sentences.en: It is able to keep track of all of OJ's alibis at once.
sentences.zh: 它能够同时追踪辛普森所有的不在场证明。

sentences.en: Pretty amazing stuff.
sentences.zh: 真是了不起的东西。

sentences.en: The product was launched with an event hosted by Jay Leno of The Tonight Show.
sentences.zh: 该产品的发布会由《今夜秀》的主持人杰伊·莱诺主持。

sentences.en: Well, Windows 95 is so easy, even a talk show host can figure it out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Windows 95太简单了，连脱口秀主持人都搞得懂。

sentences.en: As the product went on sale, the lights of the Empire State Building were changed to mirror the company's red, green, blue, and yellow logo.
sentences.zh: 产品上市时，帝国大厦的灯光变幻成了该公司红、绿、蓝、黄标志的颜色。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: This is Jennifer Aniston.
sentences.zh: 我是詹妮弗·安妮斯顿。

sentences.en: I'm Matthew Perry.
sentences.zh: 我是马修·派瑞。

sentences.en: We're here to see Mr. Bill Gates about a possible starring role in the video guide to Microsoft Windows 95.
sentences.zh: 我们来找比尔·盖茨先生，谈谈在微软Windows 95视频指南中出演主角的可能。

sentences.en: Microsoft even had a tutorial on how to use Windows that starred Jennifer Aniston and
sentences.zh: 微软甚至制作了一个关于如何使用Windows的教程，由詹妮弗·安妮斯顿和

sentences.en: Matthew Perry, who were the two lead stars of Friends, which was the most popular TV show at the time.
sentences.zh: 马修·派瑞主演，他们是当时最受欢迎的电视剧《老友记》的两大主角。

sentences.en: Task bars and email and shortcuts, oh my.
sentences.zh: 任务栏、电子邮件和快捷方式，天哪。

sentences.en: Task bars and email and shortcuts, oh my.
sentences.zh: 任务栏、电子邮件和快捷方式，天哪。

sentences.en: And Microsoft had been pumping this for months.
sentences.zh: 微软已经为此造势数月。

sentences.en: Millions of computer buffs swarmed into stores to buy the software package that's described as the dawn of a new era in personal computing.
sentences.zh: 数百万电脑迷蜂拥至商店购买该软件包，它被描述为个人计算新时代的曙光。

sentences.en: And the company then announced that it sold a million copies in the first four days.
sentences.zh: 随后该公司宣布，在头四天内售出了100万份。

sentences.en: So it's hard to understate just how pervasive Microsoft and Windows were at the time.
sentences.zh: 因此，怎么强调微软和Windows在当时的无孔不入都不为过。

sentences.en: In the midst of Microsoft's dominance, something else is emerging.
sentences.zh: 在微软占据主导地位的同时，另一股势力正在崛起。

sentences.en: And it's the early commercialization of the internet.
sentences.zh: 那就是互联网的早期商业化。

sentences.en: And remember, most people got on the internet with what was called dial-up service.
sentences.zh: 请记住，大多数人是通过所谓的拨号服务连接互联网的。

sentences.en: It was literally, you connect to a telephone landline, you know, this symphony of the calling sounds, and then the bzzz.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，你连接到固定电话线，你知道，发出呼叫的交响乐般的杂音，然后是滋滋声。

sentences.en: You know, loading early web pages, you could, you know, you could go off and get a cup of coffee and come back.
sentences.zh: 加载早期的网页，你可以，你知道，你可以去喝杯咖啡再回来。

sentences.en: It slowly came from the top of the screen and gradually filled.
sentences.zh: 它从屏幕顶部缓缓出现并逐渐填满。

sentences.en: I mean, it is an experience that today would be so broken that no one would hesitate for a moment just to junk it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种体验如果放在今天会烂到让人毫不犹豫地立刻抛弃。

sentences.en: But what you did see...
sentences.zh: 但你确实看到了……

sentences.en: An attractive, easy-to-use shop window, a gateway to the riches of the internet.
sentences.zh: 一个引人注目、易于使用的店面，通往互联网财富的大门。

sentences.en: This is a browser.
sentences.zh: 这是一个浏览器。

sentences.en: What you did see is if you typed into that small rectangular box at the top, the browser box, typed in an address ending with .com or .org, it brought you someplace for nothing.
sentences.zh: 你确实看到的是，如果你在顶部的那个小长方形框——浏览器框里输入一个以 .com 或 .org 结尾的地址，它就能免费把你带到某个地方。

sentences.en: Anything was accessible anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 世界上任何地方的东西都是触手可及的。

sentences.en: And you could see that.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这一点。

sentences.en: This is where you get finally a commercial potential challenger to Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 这就是你最终找到微软的潜在商业挑战者的地方。

sentences.en: What could possibly threaten the survival of the world's largest software company?
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么能够威胁到全球最大软件公司的生存？

sentences.en: It revolves around a part of the internet called the World Wide Web.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着互联网的一个部分展开，叫做万维网。

sentences.en: And it's this little startup company called Netscape.
sentences.zh: 这就是一家名为网景的小型初创公司。

sentences.en: Netscape was the first commercial pioneer of internet browsing software that was at all successful.
sentences.zh: 网景是第一家在互联网浏览器软件领域取得任何成功的商业先驱。

sentences.en: Netscape is engaged in a battle over whose software programs will be used to access the internet.
sentences.zh: 网景正在争夺谁的软件程序将被用来访问互联网的战斗中。

sentences.en: So far, Netscape is winning.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，网景正在取胜。

sentences.en: Its Netscape Navigator browser program dominates the market.
sentences.zh: 它的网景领航员浏览器程序占据了市场主导地位。

sentences.en: The founding software is written by two guys at the University of Illinois, a brand of Champaign, the National Computing Center,
sentences.zh: 最初的软件是由伊利诺伊大学香槟分校的两个人、国家计算中心的某个品牌编写的，

sentences.en: one of whom is Marc Andreessen, who is much better known now as one of the leading venture capitalists in Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 其中一人是马克·安德森，他现在作为硅谷领先的风险投资家之一而闻名得多。

sentences.en: At 11 a.m.
sentences.zh: 今天上午11点，

sentences.en: this morning, Netscape's stock went public and Wall Street went bonkers.
sentences.zh: 网景的股票上市，华尔街为之疯狂。

sentences.en: Initially offered at a price of $28 a share, Netscape shot up to $72 within minutes.
sentences.zh: 最初定价为每股28美元，网景在几分钟内飙升至72美元。

sentences.en: And so this company, which is basically founded in the spring of 1994, hits an IPO in August of 95, which is just, you know, rocket speed.
sentences.zh: 所以这家基本上成立于1994年春天的公司，在95年8月进行了首次公开募股，简直是以火箭般的速度。

sentences.en: And the IPO is extremely successful.
sentences.zh: 而且首次公开募股极其成功。

sentences.en: And so we have this entity that starts to just take off like wildfire.
sentences.zh: 于是我们有了这样一个开始以星火燎原之势腾飞的实体。

sentences.en: It is this first commercial wave of the internet.
sentences.zh: 这就是互联网的第一波商业浪潮。

sentences.en: And Microsoft isn't there.
sentences.zh: 而微软并不在其中。

sentences.en: I mean, this is something outside their realm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是他们领域之外的东西。

sentences.en: And so Gates, who's very technical, writes what becomes a famous memo for internal circulation within Microsoft called the internet tidal wave.
sentences.zh: 因此，技术极佳的盖茨写了一份在微软内部流传并成为著名的备忘录，题为《互联网浪潮》。

sentences.en: And he, you know, basically says it's an incredible opportunity as well as a challenge for us
sentences.zh: 他基本上表示，这对我们来说既是一个难以置信的机遇，也是一个挑战，

sentences.en: and identifies Netscape as this competitor born on the internet and their chief target.
sentences.zh: 并把网景认定为这个诞生于互联网的竞争对手以及他们的主要目标。

sentences.en: So what does Microsoft do?
sentences.zh: 那么微软做了什么？

sentences.en: Microsoft essentially goes to war with Netscape.
sentences.zh: 微软基本上向网景宣战了。

sentences.en: It starts by developing its own browser, which it calls Internet Explorer.
sentences.zh: 它首先开发了自己的浏览器，称之为Internet Explorer。

sentences.en: But for years, it's clearly an inferior product to Netscape's navigator.
sentences.zh: 但在多年里，它明显是一个逊于网景领航员的产品。

sentences.en: But Microsoft's tactics don't stop there.
sentences.zh: 但微软的策略并未止步于此。

sentences.en: Microsoft then bundles Internet Explorer into its dominant product, Windows.
sentences.zh: 随后，微软将Internet Explorer捆绑到其主导产品Windows中。

sentences.en: It charges nothing for it, so it gives it away for free, undermining Netscape's ability to charge for its browser.
sentences.zh: 它不收取任何费用，也就是免费赠送，从而破坏了网景对其浏览器收费的能力。

sentences.en: And then it goes out and uses its dominance in the personal computer industry to arrange contracts that make it very difficult for PC makers
sentences.zh: 接着，它利用在个人电脑行业的主导地位安排合同，使得个人电脑制造商很难在其电脑上

sentences.en: to feature Netscape on their personal computers.
sentences.zh: 主打网景浏览器。

sentences.en: So really kind of bare-knuckle tactics by Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的是微软采取的毫不留情的强硬战术。

sentences.en: What does Netscape do?
sentences.zh: 网景做了什么？

sentences.en: Netscape still kept doing well.
sentences.zh: 网景依然表现得很好。

sentences.en: Into 1996, they had over 80% market share of the browser business.
sentences.zh: 进入1996年，他们在浏览器业务上占据了超过80%的市场份额。

sentences.en: But the Netscape executives sort of see what's coming.
sentences.zh: 但网景的高管们某种程度上预见到了即将发生的事情。

sentences.en: Microsoft is chipping away at Netscape's lead in the browser market.
sentences.zh: 微软正在蚕食网景在浏览器市场的领先地位。

sentences.en: It has improved its browser.
sentences.zh: 它改进了自己的浏览器。

sentences.en: Microsoft has bundled it into Windows.
sentences.zh: 微软把它捆绑进了Windows。

sentences.en: It's clear that on the current path, Netscape is in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 很明显，照目前的路径走下去，网景将陷入真正的麻烦。

sentences.en: And so the leadership of Netscape talks to its outside lawyer, says, look, do your research, put together a document that we can show
sentences.zh: 于是网景的高层与他们的外部律师交谈，说，听着，做你的研究，整理出一份文件，我们可以展示

sentences.en: of all the misdeeds here and the chronology of what our rise and what Microsoft has done, and we'll take it to the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 这里的所有不当行为以及我们的崛起和微软所作所为的时间表，我们将把它提交给司法部。

sentences.en: And that white paper is over 220 pages, and it's pretty detailed.
sentences.zh: 这份白皮书长达220多页，内容相当详尽。

sentences.en: They take this white paper to the Justice Department, and that is the beginning of a landmark antitrust case, which is US v.
sentences.zh: 他们将这份白皮书提交给了司法部，这就是具有里程碑意义的反垄断案的开始，即美国诉

sentences.en: Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 微软案。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的益智游戏“纵横连线”。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天创作拼字蜜蜂和Letterboxd游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com斜杠games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: So tell me about this case, US v.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲这个案子吧，美国诉

sentences.en: Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 微软案。

sentences.en: So in May 1998...
sentences.zh: 话说在1998年5月……

sentences.en: Today we are taking another step to keep our marketplace competitive.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们正在采取又一步行动，以保持我们市场的竞争力。

sentences.en: Janet Reno, who is the head of the Justice Department, has a splashy news conference announcing they are taking on Microsoft in a huge antitrust case.
sentences.zh: 司法部长珍妮特·雷诺召开了一场轰动的记者会，宣布他们将在一个巨大的反垄断案中起诉微软。

sentences.en: Microsoft's actions have stifled competition in the operating system and browser markets.
sentences.zh: 微软的行为扼杀了操作系统和浏览器市场的竞争。

sentences.en: But most importantly, it has restricted the choices available for consumers in America and around the world.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，它限制了美国乃至全世界消费者可用的选择。

sentences.en: Months later, when the trial begins, it is pandemonium.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，当庭审开始时，现场一片混乱。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody's there to cover it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，所有人都去报道了。

sentences.en: I was told that at the New York Times, there are only three trials where we have written about every day that ran for any length.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉我，在《纽约时报》，我们连续每天报道过任何长度的庭审只有三次。

sentences.en: I mean, one was the Microsoft trial.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一次是微软案庭审。

sentences.en: The other was the OJ trial.
sentences.zh: 另一次是辛普森案庭审。

sentences.en: And the third was the Lindbergh kidnapping trial.
sentences.zh: 第三次是林德伯格绑架案庭审。

sentences.en: So it was a big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一件大事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And the trial lasted for over eight months.
sentences.zh: 而且庭审持续了八个多月。

sentences.en: There were 76 days of testimony.
sentences.zh: 有76天的证词陈述。

sentences.en: It really kind of boiled down to two essential allegations.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可以归结为两个核心指控。

sentences.en: Were the contracts that Microsoft had with personal computer makers and others, an abuse of their monopoly power by restricting the distribution for Netscape's browser.
sentences.zh: 微软与个人电脑制造商及其他机构签订的合同，是否通过限制网景浏览器的分发，滥用了其垄断力量。

sentences.en: And was bundling Microsoft's browser, Internet Explorer, with its monopoly product Windows, was that illegal?
sentences.zh: 以及将微软的浏览器Internet Explorer与其垄断产品Windows捆绑在一起，这是否违法？

sentences.en: And how was the government making that case, Steve?
sentences.zh: 政府当时是如何论证这一点的呢，史蒂夫？

sentences.en: What was it arguing exactly?
sentences.zh: 它具体争辩的是什么？

sentences.en: This was the first real email trial.
sentences.zh: 这是第一场真正的电子邮件审判。

sentences.en: The Justice Department had gathered troves and troves of memos of meetings and of email from inside Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 司法部收集了微软内部海量的会议备忘录和电子邮件。

sentences.en: And that gave you a glimpse inside how the company operated in a way it just, you know, never would have happened before.
sentences.zh: 这让你得以一窥这家公司的运作方式，在以前，你知道的，这绝对是不可能的。

sentences.en: In this email evidence and in notes that were taken at private meetings, you had the kind of phrasing like, cut off their air supply, you know, crush them, knife the baby.
sentences.zh: 在这类电子邮件证据以及私人会议的记录中，有诸如“切断他们的氧气”、“你知道的，压碎他们”、“给这婴儿一刀”这样的言论。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: The tone of this, you know, showed the kind of unrestrained competitive culture within Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种语气展现了微软内部那种肆无忌惮的竞争文化。

sentences.en: They were doing everything they possibly could.
sentences.zh: 他们竭尽所能地在做事。

sentences.en: We have to leverage Windows more because we're not going to just win with the Internet Explorer because it's not that good a product yet.
sentences.zh: 我们必须更多地利用Windows，因为我们不能仅仅靠Internet Explorer取胜，因为它作为一个产品还不够好。

sentences.en: All of this kind of came out in the email.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都在电子邮件中曝光了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there are these aggressive emails with this very kind of remarkable language.
sentences.zh: 所以有这些充满极具冲击力言辞的好斗邮件。

sentences.en: What else did the government introduce?
sentences.zh: 政府还提交了什么？

sentences.en: At the very start of the trial.
sentences.zh: 在庭审刚开始的时候。

sentences.en: I understand that you're one of the co-founders of Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 我听说你是微软的联合创始人之一。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 是这样的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What's your present title?
sentences.zh: 你目前的头衔是什么？

sentences.en: Chairman and CEO.
sentences.zh: 董事长兼首席执行官。

sentences.en: There was excerpts of videotaped deposition testimony from Bill Gates.
sentences.zh: 其中有比尔·盖茨录像视频证词的节选。

sentences.en: And he came off as he was nitpicking.
sentences.zh: 他给人的感觉是在吹毛求疵。

sentences.en: Actually, in this last answer, I had used the word believe.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在刚才的最后一个回答中，我用了“相信”这个词。

sentences.en: So you're changing the question.
sentences.zh: 所以你在偷换问题。

sentences.en: Well, if believe and conclude is different for you, I'll ask it both ways.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果“相信”和“得出结论”对你来说不同，我会用两种方式提问。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very different.
sentences.zh: 对，这有很大不同。

sentences.en: He was uncooperative.
sentences.zh: 他极不配合。

sentences.en: Do you recall receiving this memorandum or email?
sentences.zh: 你还记得收到这份备忘录或电子邮件吗？

sentences.en: Email, no.
sentences.zh: 电子邮件，不记得。

sentences.en: You don't recall receiving this email?
sentences.zh: 你不记得收到过这封电子邮件？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不记得。

sentences.en: They showed him emails.
sentences.zh: 他们向他展示了电子邮件。

sentences.en: He didn't remember any of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他对这些事情全不记着了。

sentences.en: What non-Microsoft browsers were you concerned about in January of 1996?
sentences.zh: 在1996年1月，你关心的是哪些非微软浏览器？

sentences.en: I don't know what you mean, concerned.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你说的“关心”是什么意思。

sentences.en: What is it about the word concerned that you don't understand?
sentences.zh: “关心”这个词有什么地方是你听不懂的？

sentences.en: I'm not sure what you mean by it.
sentences.zh: 我不确定你用它是什么意思。

sentences.en: Is the term concerned a term that you're familiar with in the English language?
sentences.zh: “关心”这个词是你英语里熟悉的词吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Does it have a meaning that you're familiar with?
sentences.zh: 它有一个你熟悉的含义吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But you have to understand that the reputation of this guy, and he had appeared a lot in public before, is super smart, on it, totally up to speed on everything.
sentences.zh: 但你必须明白这个家伙的声誉——他以前经常在公众露面——超级聪明，精明能干，对一切都了如指掌。

sentences.en: And this came off as dishoneSt.
sentences.zh: 而这显得很不诚实。

sentences.en: And it undermined the credibility of the Microsoft case.
sentences.zh: 这削弱了微软案辩护的可信度。

sentences.en: And put together, it was pretty damning.
sentences.zh: 综合来看，这是相当致命的。

sentences.en: And perhaps even the nature of the arrogance of the deposition sort of, like, spoke to the monopoly.
sentences.zh: 也许甚至那次作证中傲慢的态度，某种程度上也印证了垄断。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And how did Bill Gates and Microsoft respond?
sentences.zh: 那么比尔·盖茨和微软是如何回应的呢？

sentences.en: What were they arguing?
sentences.zh: 他们的辩词是什么？

sentences.en: That what they were doing was good for consumers.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的一切对消费者是有利的。

sentences.en: What's free?
sentences.zh: 什么是免费的？

sentences.en: Pro-consumer.
sentences.zh: 对消费者有利的。

sentences.en: I mean, what's better than that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有比这更好的吗？

sentences.en: They were innovating, and, you know, the government and others shouldn't get in the way.
sentences.zh: 他们在创新，而且，你知道的，政府和其他人不应该横加干涉。

sentences.en: And their strongest pushback was on the bundling.
sentences.zh: 他们最强烈的反击是在捆绑销售上。

sentences.en: Because if they couldn't bundle anything they wanted to in their operating system into Windows, that was government meddling in product design.
sentences.zh: 因为如果他们不能在操作系统Windows中捆绑他们想放进去的任何东西，那就是政府对产品设计的干预。

sentences.en: And the government should not be anywhere near this.
sentences.zh: 政府根本不应该插手此事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Microsoft said this was going to be a terrible precedent, that it could essentially allow government to meddle in the innovation economy, which Microsoft was at the forefront of.
sentences.zh: 微软表示，这将是一个糟糕的先例，它本质上可能允许政府干预创新经济，而微软正是创新经济的排头兵。

sentences.en: And they felt so strongly about this, they cast the issue in no uncertain terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们对此深信不疑，以至于毫不含糊地表态。

sentences.en: At one point, Microsoft's executive said, we can bundle anything we want into Windows, including a ham sandwich.
sentences.zh: 有一次，微软的高管说，我们可以在Windows中捆绑我们想要的任何东西，包括火腿三明治。

sentences.en: So it sounds a lot like the way Silicon Valley and the tech industry talks today about their mission, right?
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像今天硅谷和科技行业谈论其使命的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, when people criticize the tech industry, they say, we're just trying to be good, and we're just trying to do great things and help the world innovate.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道的，当人们批评科技行业时，他们会说，我们只是想做好人，我们只是想做伟大的事情并帮助世界创新。

sentences.en: And it sounds a lot to me like the arguments that are being made today.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像今天提出的那些论点。

sentences.en: You know, the government can't understand the amazing things we're doing and should not stand in our way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，政府无法理解我们正在做的惊人事情，不应该挡我们的路。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the broad phrasing of this is, we're changing the world.
sentences.zh: 用宏大的说法就是，我们正在改变世界。

sentences.en: As opposed to saying, you know, we are digital tool makers, which they are.
sentences.zh: 而不是说，你知道，我们是数字工具的制造者，而他们本来就是。

sentences.en: But if that's the case, then it invites outside scrutiny and regulation.
sentences.zh: 但如果是这样的话，就会招致外界的审视和监管。

sentences.en: How does all of this ultimately shake out?
sentences.zh: 这一切最终是如何收场的？

sentences.en: What happens in the end?
sentences.zh: 最终发生了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, after this lengthy trial, we get a ruling from the judge and he sides with the
sentences.zh: 我是说，经过这场漫长的审判，我们得到了法官的裁决，他站在了

sentences.en: Justice Department that Microsoft has abused its monopoly power and has repeatedly violated the nation's antitrust laws.
sentences.zh: 司法部一边，认为微软滥用了其垄断力量，并一再违反国家的反垄断法。

sentences.en: And the judge fairly quickly approved the Justice Department's preferred remedy, which was to split Microsoft into two companies.
sentences.zh: 法官相当迅速地批准了司法部首选的补救方案，即把微软拆分为两家公司。

sentences.en: One would be the Windows operating system and the other would be its office suite of software products, Word, PowerPoint, Excel.
sentences.zh: 一家是Windows操作系统，另一家是其办公软件产品套件，包括Word、PowerPoint、Excel。

sentences.en: And those would be separate from Microsoft Windows.
sentences.zh: 这些将与微软Windows分离开来。

sentences.en: Now, Microsoft resisted and said a breakup would be disastrous and is opposed, absolutely opposed to a breakup.
sentences.zh: 现在，微软进行了抵抗，称分拆将是灾难性的，并坚决反对、绝对反对分拆。

sentences.en: And that breakup never happens.
sentences.zh: 而那次分拆最终并没有发生。

sentences.en: First, an appeals court overrules it and sends it back to the district court.
sentences.zh: 首先，上诉法院推翻了裁决，并将其发回地方法院重审。

sentences.en: But what ultimately ends this case is a change in the political environment.
sentences.zh: 但最终结束这起案件的是政治环境的变化。

sentences.en: The Bush administration takes over from the Clinton administration.
sentences.zh: 布什政府接替了克林顿政府。

sentences.en: They're less aggressive about antitruSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在反垄断方面没那么激进。

sentences.en: And their Justice Department is ordered to engage in settlement talks with Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 他们的司法部被命令与微软进行和解谈判。

sentences.en: And they settle the case.
sentences.zh: 他们庭外和解了此案。

sentences.en: Does that mean they threw everything out?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着他们把一切都抛弃了？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: The court rulings still stand.
sentences.zh: 法院的裁决依然有效。

sentences.en: The findings of facts and the conclusion of law.
sentences.zh: 事实认定和法律结论依然存在。

sentences.en: It was a big loss for Microsoft, but it wasn't this catastrophic breakup of the company, or could have been a catastrophic breakup of the company that they had, you know, deathly
sentences.zh: 这对微软来说是一个沉重的打击，但它并不是那种毁灭性的公司分拆，或者说原本可能成为他们一直以来极为

sentences.en: feared.
sentences.zh: 恐惧的毁灭性分拆。

sentences.en: And you had restrictions placed as part of the settlement.
sentences.zh: 作为和解的一部分，你们受到了一些限制。

sentences.en: You had restrictions placed on the kinds of contracts, for example, that Microsoft could impose on industry partners.
sentences.zh: 比如，对微软可以强加给行业伙伴的合同种类施加了限制。

sentences.en: So the PC makers could feature any software they wanted to on Windows.
sentences.zh: 因此，个人电脑制造商可以在Windows上展示他们想要的任何软件。

sentences.en: And the other thing was access to some of their technology.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是访问他们的一些技术。

sentences.en: One of the concerns and the threats, the rest of the software industry is, you know, if Microsoft doesn't like you, your stuff isn't going to work very well on Windows.
sentences.zh: 其他软件行业面临的担忧和威胁之一就是，你知道的，如果微软不喜欢你，你的东西在Windows上就无法很好地运行。

sentences.en: And so this, it wasn't all opened up, but some of it was.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然没有完全开放，但部分开放了。

sentences.en: So this was not a remedy on the scale of a breakup.
sentences.zh: 因此，这不是一次达到分拆规模的补救措施。

sentences.en: What was the ultimate effect of this case in the end?
sentences.zh: 这个案件最终的深远影响是什么？

sentences.en: People debate that to this day.
sentences.zh: 人们至今仍在争论不休。

sentences.en: I mean, on one side, you have people say that had made no difference whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一方面，有人认为这完全没有产生任何影响。

sentences.en: Market sources were at work.
sentences.zh: 市场力量在起作用。

sentences.en: The Internet was developing and opening up.
sentences.zh: 互联网正在发展并开放。

sentences.en: And that the browser competition would have taken care of itself one way or another, and new innovators would have come in.
sentences.zh: 浏览器的竞争无论如何都会自行解决，新的创新者也会涌现。

sentences.en: And for Netscape, you can argue that the ruling and the outcome of the trial were too little, too late.
sentences.zh: 对于网景来说，你可以争辩说裁决和审判结果是“于事无补，为时已晚”。

sentences.en: By that time, Microsoft had really taken the upper hand in the browser market.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，微软确实已经占据了浏览器市场的上风。

sentences.en: And Netscape was eventually sold to America Online.
sentences.zh: 网景最终被卖给了美国在线。

sentences.en: And Netscape as a company went away.
sentences.zh: 而网景作为一家公司消失了。

sentences.en: So if this door opening was too late for Netscape, in a sense, it still happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这种开门对于网景来说为时已晚，从某种意义上说，它还是发生了。

sentences.en: And four months after the Microsoft trial began, a small startup called Google was founded.
sentences.zh: 在微软庭审开始四个月后，一家名为谷歌的小型初创公司成立了。

sentences.en: It had a thing called a search engine.
sentences.zh: 它有一个叫做搜索引擎的东西。

sentences.en: It had no business model.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何商业模式。

sentences.en: It had, you know, but the door was open.
sentences.zh: 它有，你知道的，但门已经打开了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: A lot of people think Microsoft became a less aggressive, less utterly unrestrained entity than it was.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为，微软变得比以前不那么激进、不再那么肆无忌惮了。

sentences.en: And that kept the door open for newcomers like Google.
sentences.zh: 这为谷歌等后起之秀敞开了大门。

sentences.en: I mean, it just all comes full circle here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切在这里形成了一个完整的闭环。

sentences.en: Google sprouted from the ground that had been made fertile by the court case against Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 谷歌萌芽于针对微软的反垄断诉讼所肥沃的土壤中。

sentences.en: It really opened the door for new companies.
sentences.zh: 它确实为新公司打开了大门。

sentences.en: And here we are today, once again, kind of in the same boat.
sentences.zh: 而今天，我们再次陷入了同样的境地。

sentences.en: But it's Google this time, not Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 但这次是谷歌，而不是微软。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you can look at Google's search engine as the equivalent of Microsoft's Windows operating system.
sentences.zh: 你可以把谷歌的搜索引擎看作是微软Windows操作系统的同等产品。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So stepping back here for a second, we know that the Microsoft case was one of the primary influences on the judge who just declared Google a monopoly.
sentences.zh: 所以退一步讲，我们知道微软案是对刚刚宣判谷歌为垄断企业的法官的主要影响因素之一。

sentences.en: We're still waiting, of course, to see what remedies that judge ultimately recommends.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们仍在等待，看看那位法官最终会提出什么救济建议。

sentences.en: But I wonder how you think the Microsoft case might shape where that judge lands in the end.
sentences.zh: 不过我想知道，你认为微软案会如何影响这位法官最终的裁决。

sentences.en: Like, what clues does it give us here?
sentences.zh: 比如，它能给我们提供什么线索？

sentences.en: Well, we have a whole separate hearing on remedies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还有一场专门关于救济措施的听证会。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of proposals, everything from just restricting certain contracts, banning
sentences.zh: 而且有很多提案，从仅仅限制某些合同、禁止

sentences.en: those kinds of payments to having to split off either its Android operating system or its
sentences.zh: 这类付款，到必须拆分其安卓操作系统或

sentences.en: Chrome browser.
sentences.zh: Chrome浏览器。

sentences.en: We have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我们完全不知道。

sentences.en: But what I think you have here is a signal of what kind of behavior in this environment is going to be viewed as suspect and what you should avoid.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你在这里看到的是一个信号，表明在这种环境下，什么样的行为会被视为可疑，以及你应该避免什么。

sentences.en: And again, a lot of debate about these antitrust cases, you know, whether they're worthwhile or not.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，关于这些反垄断案有很多争论，你知道的，探讨它们是否值得。

sentences.en: But I think what you do have is a sense of some restraining influence on these dominant companies, some pulling back and some opening of the door to opportunity for innovators.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你确实感受到了一些对这些主导企业的制约力量，一些收敛，以及为创新者打开机遇之门。

sentences.en: And we don't know what the future is going to look like or who is going to benefit.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不知道未来会是什么样子，也不知道谁会受益。

sentences.en: I mean, one irony is that a winner could be Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个具有讽刺意味的是，赢家可能是微软。

sentences.en: It has the most directly competing search engine to Google with Bing.
sentences.zh: 它拥有与谷歌搜索引擎竞争最直接的必应（Bing）。

sentences.en: But I think the broader implication is the uncertainty of new innovation and trying to keep the door open for the kind of things you may not have thought about.
sentences.zh: 但我认为更广泛的意义在于新创新的不确定性，并努力为那些你可能没有想到的事情敞开大门。

sentences.en: Just as nobody thought Google would become what it did when it was founded in the midst of the
sentences.zh: 正如当谷歌在微软

sentences.en: Microsoft trial.
sentences.zh: 诉讼案期间创立时，没有人会想到它会发展成今天的样子。

sentences.en: You don't know what the future is going to hold, but you want that window of opportunity,
sentences.zh: 你不知道未来会怎样，但你希望有那扇机遇之窗，

sentences.en: that door to be opened so that whatever comes, it has a better chance of success than it might have had otherwise.
sentences.zh: 那扇敞开的大门，这样无论发生什么，它比原本更有可能成功。

sentences.en: Which is fundamentally what these cases are about.
sentences.zh: 这正是这些案件的根本所在。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Steve, thank you.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Hamas announced that it would not take part in a long-awaited round of ceasefire talks with Israel planned for Thursday, despite stepped-up pressure from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周二，哈马斯宣布将不参加原定于周四举行的与以色列备受期待的新一轮停火谈判，尽管美国施加了越来越大的压力

sentences.en: to reach a deal.
sentences.zh: 以达成协议。

sentences.en: A representative for Hamas in Lebanon said in an interview that Hamas had decided not to
sentences.zh: 哈马斯驻黎巴嫩代表在接受采访时表示，哈马斯决定不参加

sentences.en: participate because its leaders did not think the Israeli government had been negotiating in good faith.
sentences.zh: 是因为其领导人认为以色列政府没有进行诚意谈判。

sentences.en: The decision came after the Times reported that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had
sentences.zh: 此前有媒体报道称，以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡

sentences.en: quietly added new conditions that negotiators fear have created extra obstacles to a deal.
sentences.zh: 悄悄增加了新的条件，谈判代表担心这给达成协议制造了额外的障碍。

sentences.en: Netanyahu's office has denied that he added new conditions and said that he was simply seeking to clarify ambiguities.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡办公室否认他增加了新条件，并表示他只是在寻求澄清模棱两可之处。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Ricky Nevetsky, Rochelle Bonja, and Sidney Harper, with help from Nina Feldman.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由里基·内韦茨基（Ricky Nevetsky）、罗谢尔·邦贾（Rochelle Bonja）和西德尼·哈珀（Sidney Harper）制作，尼娜·费尔德曼（Nina Feldman）协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, contains original music by Diane Wong, Alicia Bitt-YouTube, Dan Powell, and Pat McCusker, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 节目由马克·乔治（Mark George）剪辑，包含黛安·黄（Diane Wong）、艾丽西亚·比特-YouTube（Alicia Bitt-YouTube）、丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）和帕特·麦克库斯克（Pat McCusker）的原创音乐，并由艾莉莎·莫克斯利（Alyssa Moxley）进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰斯伯格（Ben Landsberg）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《今日》（The Daily）的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西（Sabrina Tavernisi）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《都市》（Metro）的最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格（Sarah Koenig）将为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
